Which Touring Bike Do You Need?

Choosing the right touring motorcycle can be overwhelming with so many categories and models available. Our visual decision tree simplifies the process with five simple questions that guide you to the perfect bike type for your riding style.

The Five Categories

  • Adventure Tourer — For riders who venture off-road with heavy luggage. Think BMW R1250GS and Triumph Tiger 1200. These handle motorways and green lanes equally well.
  • Dual Sport — Lighter off-road capability without the heavy touring luggage. Honda Africa Twin and KTM 890 Adventure are perfect for riders who prioritise trails over panniers.
  • Full Dresser — Maximum comfort for long motorway miles with a pillion. Honda Gold Wing and BMW K1600GTL are the kings of effortless distance with every luxury included.
  • Sport Tourer — Fast motorway touring with a sportier edge. Kawasaki Ninja 1000SX and Yamaha Tracer 9 GT blend performance with practical touring ability.
  • Naked Tourer — Versatile machines for riders who avoid motorways and prefer B-roads. Triumph Tiger Sport 660 and Suzuki GSX-S1000GT offer upright comfort with character.

Still unsure? Use our Gear Finder to match accessories to your chosen bike, or explore the best roads to ride on our UK Biker Road Ratings page.
keyTakeaways: The decision tree sorts touring bikes into five clear categories based on your riding style.
Adventure tourers like the BMW R1250GS suit riders mixing motorways with green lanes.
Full dressers such as the Honda Gold Wing prioritise pillion comfort over long distances.
Sport tourers blend performance with practicality for fast motorway miles.
Naked tourers reward riders who favour B-roads and upright comfort over motorway cruising.

faq.q: What type of touring bike should a beginner buy?
faq.a: Many new tourers do well on a naked tourer or a middleweight adventure bike. Models like the Triumph Tiger Sport 660 offer upright comfort, manageable weight and enough luggage capacity for weekends without the bulk of a full dresser. Test-ride a few categories before committing.

faq.q: What is the difference between an adventure tourer and a dual sport?
faq.a: An adventure tourer is built to carry heavy luggage and cover big miles on tarmac while still handling green lanes, such as the BMW R1250GS. A dual sport is lighter and more trail-focused, like the KTM 890 Adventure, trading some luggage capacity and motorway comfort for genuine off-road ability.

faq.q: Is a full dresser worth it for solo riders?
faq.a: Full dressers like the Gold Wing shine when carrying a pillion over long motorway distances, offering luxury, weather protection and comfort. Solo riders who mostly enjoy B-roads may find them heavy and unwieldy. If you rarely ride two-up, a sport tourer or naked tourer is usually a better fit.

faq.q: Which category is best for UK B-roads?
faq.a: Naked tourers and middleweight adventure bikes excel on twisty British B-roads. Their upright riding position, torquey engines and lighter weight make them easy to flick through corners and enjoyable at legal speeds, unlike heavier full dressers that prefer sweeping motorway miles.

faq.q: How many miles can these bikes tour comfortably?
faq.a: All five categories are capable of multi-day touring, but comfort varies. Full dressers and sport tourers handle 300-plus mile days with ease thanks to fairings and larger tanks, while naked tourers are happiest with regular stops every 90 minutes or so. Match the category to your typical daily distance.
